monthly_review.summary: Running volume collapsed this month (4.5 km vs 78.5 km), pace improved slightly but on minimal data, and zone distribution shifted sharply toward Z3 — likely reflecting either a single hard effort or measurement artifact given the absence of corroborating intensity metrics.
monthly_review.highlight: The 95% drop in monthly volume — from 78.5 km to just 4.5 km — is not a blip but a full cessation of training, confirmed across all months_back showing consistent activity until September, then near-zero output in October; this strongly indicates an external disruption (e.g., injury, illness, or burnout), not a planned taper.

goal_tracker.message: Chasing last month’s volume is medically inadvisable given the compromised readiness status and complete lack of recovery metrics — attempting to make up 74 km in 30 days would require >2.4 km/day and risk injury or relapse; focus instead on rebuilding consistency and monitoring recovery signals first.

insights.title: Z3 dominance without Z4/Z5 support suggests inefficient effort allocation
insights.body: This month’s run was 49% Z3 despite zero Z4/Z5 time — unusual for a single 4.5 km run at 7:48/km (468 sec/km); normally such pace would elicit more Z4 contribution unless HR zones are miscalibrated or effort was highly variable.

insights.title: Running economy worsened despite lower volume and higher cadence
insights.body: Avg efficiency rose from 14.58 to 15.15 ml/kg/km (worse) even as cadence increased +9 spm and aerobic TE improved — indicating possible form breakdown or fatigue-induced compensation, especially given vertical oscillillation stable at ~8.3–8.4 cm but ground contact time not available for validation.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling remained stable (2.4–3.1%) despite declining VO2max trend
insights.body: Recent runs show aerobic TE between 2.4–3.1%, well under 5% threshold, yet VO2max declined from 42.0 (Sep 15) to 41.0 (Sep 22 onward) — suggesting early aerobic deconditioning masked by preserved endurance efficiency, a classic sign of detraining onset.

insights.title: Stride length increased +6.5 cm while ground contact time is unreported
insights.body: Stride length rose from 77.97 cm (Sep 20) to 86.49 cm (Sep 24) — a 11% jump — with no ground contact time data to assess whether this reflects power gain or overstriding; vertical oscillillation held steady at 8.1–8.6 cm, making inefficiency unlikely but injury risk uncertain.

recommendations.action: Complete a 20-minute Zone 1 walk or easy spin (HR <120 bpm) on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday — no running allowed
recommendations.reason: Zero recovery metrics are available; low-intensity non-impact movement supports autonomic reset without adding load

recommendations.action: Log sleep duration and subjective energy each morning for 7 days using a simple notebook — no apps or wearables required
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is a primary missing driver of readiness; objective tracking must begin before any load reintroduction

recommendations.action: Perform daily 5-minute HRV-guided box breathing (4-4-4-4) upon waking, using free Breathly app or timer
recommendations.reason: HRV is absent from dataset but trainable via vagal stimulation; this builds readiness infrastructure before HRV measurement resumes

risk_flags.evidence: VO2max dropped from 42.0 to 41.0 across September, and zero running in October — typical 0.5–1.0 point/month decline becomes clinically meaningful with no counterbalancing stimulus
risk_flags.action: Reintroduce running only after 3 consecutive days of ≥7h sleep and subjective energy ≥6/10

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence increased +9 spm while efficiency worsened (+0.57 ml/kg/km) and stride length jumped +6.5 cm in 4 days — suggests forced turnover to maintain pace amid fatigue or reduced force production
risk_flags.action: Delay running until cadence stabilizes within ±2 spm of September’s 146 spm average

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish autonomic and perceptual feedback loops before reloading — prioritize nervous system regulation, sleep consistency, and mindful movement over distance or pace.
